MASONIC HOMES

Your Committee on Finance has reviewed the report of the Board
of Trustees of the Masonic Homes, as well as the Auditor's report on the
operations of the Homes for the year ending July 31, 1948. The Trustees

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

277

are again to be commended for their stewardship of these two fine institutions.
As pointed out in the report of the Board of Trustees, the finances
of the Homes, which have been· in such excellent condition in the past
several years, have now shrunk to where it is again necessary to ask the
Lodges for assistance in supporting the Homes.
Since 1945, when the first 50c per capita tax for the support of the
Homes was dropped, the gross income of the Homes has been reduced
from over $600,000 to $417,000, while operating expenses have continually increased and have gone from $245,000 in 1945 to $445,000 in the
year just past, leaving an operating deficit of $27,000 for the year.
The Trustees recommend that there be a per capita levy of 25c for
the operation of the Homes and an additional 25c for the Building Fund
for the year beginning August 1, 1949, and your Committee on Finance
concurs in that recommendation.
Your Committee therefore offers the following Resolution and moves
its adoption:
Resolved: That a per capita of 25c be levied for the operations of the
Masonic Homes; and that an additional per capita of 25c be levied for
the Building Fund of the Masonic Homes.
MASONIC HOMES ENDOWMENT BOARD

The sixteenth report of this Board is as usual very interesting. It
indicates that contributions through the Lodges increased the Endowment Fund by $187,000 and that bequests increased it by over $200,000,
a total increase of approximately $400,000, making a total of $3,300,000
at the close of the fiscal year.
The progress that has been made during the sixteen years of existence of the Board is indeed remarkable. An increase of $2,750,000 in the
Endowment Fund, with an expenditure through the appropriation of
Grand Lodge Fund of about $100,000, is a tribute to the enthusiasm.
hard work and intelligent planning of those who have served as members
of the Board and particularly of those who have served as chairmen.
The graphs in the report and which were shown on slides at the
presentation of the report are both revealing and realistic. While they
show remarkable progress they indicate also, that the expenses of the
Homes are increasing at a far greater rate than the increase of income
from the greatly accelerated Endowment Fund and that what may have
seemed to be a very satisfactory goal for an Endowment Fund ten years
ago is now entirely out of proportion.
We feel, therefore, that interest and enthusiasm in this work must
not lag and that the Endowment Board must be given every encouragement by the Grand Lodge.
At the 1947 Communication of Grand Lodge, $8,000 was appropriated for the use of the Endowment Board, of which approximately

COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC SCHOOLS WEEK

The annual observance of Public Schools Week has become a fixed
activity of the Grand Lodge of California. It has proven to be an
activity which is causing favorable comment by many of the Masonic
Jurisdictions throughout the world.
The observance was recommended by Past Grand Master Charles
Albert Adams while Grand Master. This Most Worshipful Brother
has headed the activities of the committee during all the years since. It
has been due to his great interest in the public schools and his forceful
handling of the committee that the observance has become such an outstanding activity.
Each year the chairman finds it necessary to be to some expense in
caring for the various duties of the committee. Last year there was
appropriated, at the request of the Chairman, $1,250. The expenses of
the Committee amounted to $745.36.
The Chairman this year estimates that there will be needed in carrying on the activities of the Committee the sum of $1,250.00. Your Committee on Finance approves the request and recommends the appropriation.

GRAND LODGE ACTIVITIES WEEK

The work of the Activities Committee, under the able guidance of
Andrew Burke, has again very effectually accomplished the purpose for
which it is organized. The annual get-together dinner, attended by 1121
members of Grand Lodge, the entertainment of Grand Lodge Officers,
Distinguished Guests, their Ladies and Grand Lodge Members, as. well
as the annual pilgrimage to the Decoto Home, were all accomplished
with a great deal of graciousness and efficiency.
Your Committee on Finance recommends that the sum of $5,000 be
appropriated for the purpose of paying the ex~enses co~tr_a~ted for. by
this committee in carrying out the aforementioned activities, subiect
to various items being audited in the usual manner.
The Committee on Grand Lodge Activities Week is of the opinion
that the amount of $5,000 will be sufficient to take care of the various
activities one year hence. No appropriation is being recommended at
this time to cover these expenses, as the entire expenditure occurs
after the close of the regular Grand Lodge year, July 31, 1949. However, it is understood that these expenses are to be incurred and that
some of them will have to be paid prior to the Annual Communication
of Grand Lodge. Such expenses are hereby authorized and will be
included in the appropriations made at the next session of Grand Lodge.
COMMITTEE ON CORRESPONDENCE

Special acclaim should be given this committee who, under the able
chairmanship of Brother James K. Fisk, has compiled a report of outstanding events in Freemasonry, both domestic and foreign, that are
truly enlightening and educational. A study of this report will at once
show the reader that an exhaustive amount of research has been done
by the committee to bring you the facts therein contained.
The Chairman of the committee wishes it known that the work of
compiling this material was apportioned among the members of the
committee so that no phase would he overlooked. This resulted in only
$35.00 of the appropriation of $250.00 allotted for the purpose being
used.
It is recommended that every member of the Craft avail himself of
the opportunity of perusing this work. He will find it not only interesting but also highly educational. It is further recommended that the
Grand Secretary notify each Lodge that copies of this excellent book
are available to the members at their request.
The Chairman of the committee suggests an appropriation of $250.00
for the use of the committee for the coming year.

LODGE FINANCING COMMITTEE

This is a hard working committee and one that is doing a work of
great benefit to the Lodges. It is deserving of much praise. The report
of the Committee displays a great amount of work done, but does not
commence to show the tremendous amount of detail required and the
careful study and sound judgment that must constantly be exercised.
The Chairman of the Committee, the Worshipful Walter S. Berger,

GRAVEL RANGE LODGE NO. 59

( Situate at Camptonville)
There was appropriated at the last annual session of Grand Lodge,
for the purpose of assisting the above Lodge in rebuilding its temple
which had been destroyed by fire, the sum of $13,000. Of this amount
the Lodge found it necessary to utilize $12,578.
The new temple has been completed and is now occupied by the
Lodge.
It was not determined by your Committee on Finance at the time
the appropriation was made whether this amount was to be regarded
as an advance to said Lodge, or an outright gift. The amount is now
carried on the records of Grand Lodge as "owing from Gravel Range
Lodge."
This Commitfee has previously taken the position, which it now
renews, that all Lodges should stand on their own basis and pay any
advances of this character as far as their financial means will permit.
At this time your Committee concludes it is too early to determine what
amount of the above advance should be eventually returned by Gravel
Range Lodge. It therefore recommends the continuance of the charge
as now carried, as an advance to this Lodge.

GEORGETOWN LODGE NO. 25

It is also to be borne in mind that the second set of regalia, which
is the set used when it is necessary to ship regalia to outside communities for the purpose of cornerstone laying and other Grand Lodge ceremonies, is in an unsatisfactory condition. This would mean that should
a new set be purchased the present set of official regalia could be used
for this latter purpose.
If a new set is purchased it should be available for the Centennial
Celebration and to be available at that time it will be necessary to place
the order now, The regalia houses advise that they cannot commence
to guarantee a satisfactory job of this character much under two years.
Should it be found necessary to order a new set, it will be required to
make the appropriation at this time, as a firm commitment will have to
be made if the regalia is ordered.
Discussions have been held with various regalia houses and the
best price quoted, which -contains assurances of a satisfactory quality, is
$140.00 per set. As 26 sets are necessary it means an appropriation
of $3,640.
This Committee is therefore recommending an appropriation of the
above amount, it being understood that the appropriation is only to be
used in case it is found that the present regalia cannot be properly
cleaned and reconditioned and also with the recommendation that the
appropriation shall continue in effect over the next Grand Lodge period.

NORTHEAST LODGE NO. 255
(Situate at Fort Bidwell)
The report of the Grand Master on the need of these two Lodges
for financial help, due to loss of their temples by fire, was referred
jointly to the Committee on Policy and General Purposes and the
Committee on Finance.
A conference between the two committees has been held.
Your Committee on Finance is in accord with the report made by
the Committee on Policy and General Purposes.
Since the above portion of the report of the Finance Committee had
been prepared, the attention of the Committee has been called to the
action of Grand Lodge on the report made on the above subject by the
Committee on Policy and General Purposes.
It is therefore obvious to this Committee that unless some action is
taken by Grand Lodge at this session, these two Lodges will be compelled to forego any action on the construction of new temples and
will thereby be without places of meeting until the next session of
Grand Lodge.
It is the considered opinion of this Committee that some method of
relief should be determined upon. It therefore recommends that it be
left to the incoming Grand Master, to the Chairman of the Committee
on Finance and the Chairman of the Committee on Lodge Financing,
to determine the mount of assistance which shall be rendered to each
of these two distressed Lodges, it being understood that the final disposition, that is, whether it is to be an advance or an outright gift shall
in each case be left to the determination of the Finance Committee at
the next session of Grand Lodge.
Your Committee on Finance recommends whatever amounts may
be determined upon by the above committees, for the assistance to
Georgetown Lodge No. 25 and Northeast Lodge No. 266, be appropriated.

ADVANCES FOR OTHER JURISDICTIONS

In the report of this Committee a year ago there was shown due this
Grand Lodge from the Masonic Jurisdictions outside the United States
advances as follows:
Grand Lodge A. F. & A. M. of Scotland.......... $1,000.00
This item represents an advance made by the Board of Relief of
San Francisco in 1942 for the benefit of the wife of William Johnstone,
a member of Lodge St. John Selkirk No. 32-Scotland. The amount
was paid out by the Board of Relief on authorization of the Grand
Lodge of Scotland, the sum to repay having been deposited with them.
Due to restrictions placed by the British Government on the sending
of money out of the Empire, the Grand Lodge of Scotland has not been
able to remit the amount to this Grand Lodge. Recent requests have
been made and denied. It is obviously uncertain, due to economic conditions there, as to when this sum will be received.
Economic conditions in the British Isles have placed on Masonry
there and particularly on relief needs a very great strain. Both Brother
Johnstone, who made this deposit and the Grand Lodge of Scotland,
would welcome the contribution of the amount to their charitable needs.
It is, therefore, the recommendation of your Committee on Finance
that this $1,000 be contributed to the Scottish Masonic Benevolence
Centenary Fund.

The Special Committee on the George Washington Masonic National Memorial recommends that a levy of fifteen cents ( 15c) per
capita be made again this year and that the proceeds resulting therefrom, together with all accumulated funds of this nature on hand as at
January 15, 1949, be paid to the George Washington Masonic National

Your Committee on Finance has revised that portion of the Grand
Master's Address, referring to the creation of a Masonic Memorial
Temple to house Grand Lodge; and also the report of the Memorial
Building Committee, which has been investigating the various ramifications concerning the erection of such a temple.
The Memorial Building Committee states in its report it has not
been able to determine sufficient facts to make a recommendation to
Grand Lodge at this time concerning the erection of a Masonic Memorial Temple, and requests that the Committee be continued in order
to complete its studies and asks for sufficient funds for the purpose.
It is recognized that in order to complete its report the Memorial
Building Committee will have to make certain expenditures, such as
obtaining options on land, procuring preliminary plans and cost estimates on the building, etc. The amount of these expenditures is necessarily unknown and cannot, therefore, be accurately budgeted. There
is now on hand in Grand Lodge the sum of $158,507.44 transferred from
the War Relief Fund at the last Communication. It is the recommendation of your Committee on Finance that this reserve be made available
to the Memorial Building Committee for the purpose of completing its
report to Grand Lodge on the feasibility of the erection of a Masonic
Memorial Temple, expenditures from which shall be made upon approval
of a committee, consisting of the Grand Master, the Deputy Grand
Master and Chairman of Committee on Finance.
The Committee on Finance is not now in approval or disapproval of

PLAQUE FOR WESTERN STAR LODGE NO. 2
There has been referred to your Committee on Finance the report
of the Committee on Policy and General purposes, on the resolution
presented by Alfreci F. Ross, Past Master of Reading Lodge No. 254,
proposing that Grand Lodge present to Western Star Lodge No. 2 a
congratulatory plaque in commemoration of its Centennial observance
this year. The resolution has the approval of the Policy Committee.
While your Committee on Finance has the very highest respect
for the conclusions of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes
and is genuinely embarrassed that it cannot concur in this recommendation, and yet, it must be recognized that eventually there will be 600
Lodges eligible for memorials from Grand Lodge of some character and
that by granting this request it is establishing a precedent and probably
starting a parade for applications to Grand Lodge for plaques or memorials of some character.
This Committee is refusing to recommend an appropriation for the
building of the Columbia Memorial Temple. While this application
means a much smaller amount, yet this Committee views it that the two
applications are of a memorial character.
Your Committee on Finance therefore is constrained to disapprove
the appropriation of the necessary amount.

COLUMBIA TEMPLE RESTORATION

Your Committee on Finance has thoughtfully and thoroughly considered the report of the Columbia Temple Restoration Committee, as
referred to it by Grand Lodge Tuesday.
It will be recalled that at the last Communication of Gran-0 Lodge
your Committee on Finance suggested that the project was prematurely
presented and recommended that the Columbia Temple Restoration
Committee obtain all the information necessary to present a complete
picture to Grand Lodge at this Communication, covering plans and
specifications. costs, the possibility of State assistance in building and
maintaining the Temple, etc. This information the Committee has thoroughly and scrupulously secured. The members of the Committee are to
be commended for their thoroughness and Grand Lodge is indebted to
them for their fine work.
The cost of restoration of the Temple is estimated at $37,103 for
the reconstruction of the building and $1101 for the furnishings and
equipment, which would have to be bought, the remainder having been .
donated by Lodges throughout the Jurisdiction, and the Committee
requests an appropriation of that amount.
Without doubting that the restoration of the Columbia Temple
would provide a fine historical monument to Masonry in the old Mother
Lode country. there is considerable <loubt in the minds of your Committee on Finance as to the propriety of reconstructing this Temple,
both by reason of its being monumental only, there being no active
Lodge there to use it and also, in considering where this road may lead
us once we have elected to reconstruct Masonic Temples in historic
places, as monuments to the Craft.

The Committee on Centennial Arrangements is to be congratulated
on the report which it has prepared. While the report must, of necessity,
be fragmentary in its details it presents the broad outline of a plan
which, if perfected, should give us a Centennial celebration which will
be in keeping with the dignity and the importance of this Grand Lodge.
Your Committee on Finance is in sympathy with and recommends
the adoption of the plan as thus far outlined by the Centennial Arrangements Committee. In doing so it recognizes the ability, sincerity and
business acumen of the brothers now comprising the Committee and
feels certain that should any changes or replacements be made by succeeding Grand Masters, the members of this Grand Lodge may still

290

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

have the utmost confidence that its funds which may be entrusted to
the Committee will be expended with care and with the most satisfactory
results. We are entering into a new undertaking and while $145,000
may seem to be a very large sum to be spent on a celebration, yet as
the Committee truly points out we have no way of knowing what conditions may prevail two years from now. It is better to have ample
funds on hand and not spend them, than to fail to provide an adequate
celebration through lack of necessary funds.
Your Committee on Finance, therefore, presents the following resolution and moves its adoption:

the accounts of Grand Lodge to be added to the Centennial Fund to
cover the costs of the Centennial Celebration in 1950.
Second, tha t to provide for continuous service of the Centennial Arrangements Committee the members be appointed, for a period of three
years.
Third, that the Committee be authorized to make contracts and
commitments for such necessary expenditures, including salaries and
wages, of funds made available by the per capita tax of 25c, to conduct
and manage a Centennial Celebration that will be creditable to Grand
Lodge.
Fourth, that the Grand Secretary be authorized to honor warrants
against the Centennial fund, which may be drawn from time to time
by the Committee on Centennial Arrangements.

GRAND MASTER'S RECOMMENDATION ON GRAND LODGE RESERVES

That portion of the Grand Master's annual message deai.ing with
Grand Lodge Reserves has been referred to your Committee on Finance
and has had its consideration. The Committee is thoroughly in accord
with the Grand Master's position on Reserves.

It has long been the financial policy of the Finance Committee that
the reserves should be accumulated during the good years for the purpose of being leaned upon in stressful years. The following scheduled
reserves, together with per capita levy since 1906, is being submitted
for your information. From this it will be noted how the reserves have
gone up during the good years and have been loaned upon during the
stressful years.
It is to be particularly noted of the gradual increase since the year
1939 and at the present time the total available liquid reserve is
$526,854.54.
It is the intent of the Finance Committee to gradually add to this
reserve when it can be done without a burden on the constituent Lodges.
It must, however, be constantly born in mind that the high cost of .
operation has also hit the constituent Lodges and it is essential that no
more additional per capita should be required of them than is necessary
for the proper maintenance of Grand Lodge.

It is noted that the estimated cost of operation for the fiscal year
commencing August 1, 1948, as set out in the budget just submitted
is $266,184.58.
There is now in the treasury, for the purpose of caring for these
expenses, the sum of $187,665.00. This is from the returns of the
Lodges for the year just closed. There will also be coming in during the
year and available for expenditure, an additional amount from interest
and dividends, and some other smaJl items of income, in the sum of

approximately $32,000 making a total estimated income for the year
of $219,665.
According to this estimate of Income and Expenses, there should
be a deficit in the ytar's operations of approximately $46,519.58.
The Committee's estimate of the amount which should be received
from the per capita levy already established and from other sources of

subject and we are in entire sympathy with its finding and recommendations ..
We agree that policy should be adopted of protecting and restoring
for future generations, evidence of early day Masonry in California. We
therefore approve the recommendations of the Columbia Temple Restoration Committee.
A motion prevailed that the report be amended by striking therefrom the concluding sentence: "We therefore approve the recommendation of the Columbia Temple Restoration Committee", and the report
as amended was adopted.
The Finance Committee then moved that no appropriation be made
for the purpose of restoring Columbia Temple.
The Columbia Temple Restoration Committee offered a substitute
motion, "That the sum of $38,204.00 be appropriated for the restoration
of Columbia Temple", and by a vote of 524 in favor to 402 against, the
substitute motion carried, and Grand Lodge ordered an appropriation
of $38,204.00 for the restoration of Columbia Temple.
The Finance Committee then moved that an additional 20c per
capita be levied to provide the amount of the appropriation, and a substitute motion was offered that the appropriation be made out of the
reserves of Grand Lodge. By a vote of 507 in favor, to 360 against, the
substitute motion carried and Grand Lodge ordered that $38,204.00 for
the restoration of Columbia Temple be made from the reserves of Grand
Lodge.
The Columbia Temple Committee then moved the adoption of
recommendations 3, 4 and 5 of that report noting the correction of the
amount to $38,204.00, and the motion was carried.
In the matter of the plaque for Western Star Lodge No. 2, the Committee on Finance recommended against an appropriation. The Committee on Policy and General Purposes having approved. and Grand
Lodge having adopted the resolution as a matter of policy. the Grand
Master held that it was incumbent upon the committee to report the
appropriation to Grand Lodge. The Committee on Finance moved that
the Grand Master be authorized to direct the preparation and presentation of an appropriate plaque and to expend such amount as might be
determined by him, and the motion was carried.

In the matter of the Columbia Temple Restoration, Grand Lodge
took the following action:
The Finance Committee reported adversely on the request of the
Columbia Temple Committee for an appropriation of $38,204.00 for the
restoration of Columbia Temple. A discussion developed the fact that
the Committee on Policy and General Purposes had not made a definite
recommendation on the subject and the Grand Master re-referred the
matter back to that committee for study and directed that it make a
definite recommendation. That committee reported as follows:

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge of California:
Your committee on Policy and General Purposes, to which has been
referred the report and recommendations of the Columbia Temple Restoration Committee, reports as follows:
We have carefully considered the report as written and agree with
the proponents that much of California's early Masonic history is to be
found in the mountain sections of Northern California, commonly referred to as the Mother Lode. that unless some of these relics of pioneer
Masonry are preserved for posterity. the time will come, in the not too
distant future when all physical evidence of early day Masonry will have
disappeared.
We realize that this committee has made_an exhaustive study of the

Past Grand Master
At the close of the morning session, P. G. M. Arthur S. Crites revealed to Grand Lodge that for a long period of time he had contemplated giving up his respo:tisibility as Chairman of the Committee on Finance,
and that several months ago he had reached a definite decision to do so
at the conclusion of this Annual Communication. He made it clear to

298

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

299

AFTERNOON SESSION .

Grand Lodge that this irrevocable decision had been reached only after
long and careful consideration, and he left Grand Lodge no alternative
but to accept his decision.
A standing ovation was tendered Brother Crites for his long service
on the committee and a motion was unanimously carried that a special
committee be appointed by the Grand Master to draft a suitable resolution of appreciation, the committee to report prior to the close of this
Communication of Grand Lodge.
The Grand Master appointed Past Grand Masters John Stewart
Ross and William B. Ogden, and Brother Henry C. Clausen.

Grand ·L odge called on at 2:30 p.m. the Grand Master presiding.
Dr. H. C. Mei, Past District Grand Master of the Grand Lodge of
the Philippine Islands for China, was presented by the Grand Master
and spoke briefly expressing appreciation for the service rendered by
this Grand Lodge during the war.

Committees Discharged
The Grand Master discharged the Committees on Freedom Train
and Homes Applications, their work having been completed, and the
Committee on Accounts, superseded by professional auditors, expressing
to the members of all these Committees the thanks of Grand Lodge for
work well done.
Record is here made that portions of the reports of the committees
on Grievances, Policy and General Purposes, Jurisprudence and Finance
were made on days other than herein indicated, and in a different sequence, the complete reports having been compiled as printed for purposes of ready reference.
At 1 :05 p.m. Grand Lodge called off till 2:30 p.m.

t

Resolution
The Special Committee appointed by the Grand Master to draft
A Resolution relative to Past Grand Master Arthur S. Crites reported
as follows:
Whereas, Most Worshipful Arthur S. Crites, Past Grand Master
of Masons in California, has served this Grand Lodge long and faithfully, and Whereas, he has been a member, and for sixteen years he has
been Chairman of the Grand Lodge Committee on Finance, during
which time, by his devotion to Masonry and by the application of his
preemiJ?.ent ability as a financier he has so formed and developed our
financial program as to enhance greatly the· growth and stability of our
institution, and
Whereas, our Most Worshipful Brother has announced his irrevocable intention to retire from many of his activities, and in particular to
retire as Chairman of our Committee on Finance,
Now, Therefore, Be It Resolved, by the Most Worshipful Grand
Lodge of Free and Accepted Masons of the State of California, in its
99th Annual Communication assembled, does express to Most Worshipful Arthur S. Crites, Past Grand Master, our sincere recognition
and deep appreciation of his outstanding service to Masonry, and to
this Grand Lodge in particular, that he has earned and merits an enduring place in Masonic history throughout the Masonic world, and the
love and affection which his Brethren will always bear toward our distinguished Brother, and
Be is further Resolved that this resolution be spread upon the
Minutes of this Grand Lodge, and that a copy suitably engrossed be
presented to him at a proper time and ceremony.
Done in open Grand Lodge this 15th day of October, A. L. 5948.
Adopted unanimously followed by a standing ovation.

The M. W. Arthur S. Crites acted as Master of Ceremonies, and the
officers elected and appointed were installed by the retiring Grand
Master in due and ancient form.
The newly#installed Grand Master then invested his predecessor
with a Past Grand Master's lapel button.
The Chas. Albert Adams insignia was transferred from the retiring
to the incumbent Grand Master and the other chair officers exchanged
the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins.
The Chester H. Warlow Grand Lecturer's insignia was presented
to the incumbent Grand Lecturer by Brother Warlow, who explained
that the gold of which the lapel button was made had been mined by him
and that this insignia of office, designed by him, was to be worn by
successors in office to the Grand Lecturer.
The M. W. John R. Moore. Past Grand Master, invested the re#
tiring Grand Master with the apron of a Past Grand Master.
The M. W. Lloyd E. Wilson, Past Grand Master. on behalf of the
members of Grand Lodge presented a gift to Mrs. Chester H. Warlow,
and it was accepted by the retiring Grand Master in her behalf.
The Very Reverand James M. Malloch, on behalf of the appointive
officers who had served under Grand Master Chester H. Warlow,
presented the retiring Grand Master with a gift as a token and memento
of their appreciation of appointment and joy in having served with him.
At 5:45 p.m., all business being completed. Grand Lodge was closed
in due form.

September 23, 1948

Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California
San Francisco, California
Gentlemen
We have audited the books of account and records of the Grand Lodge
F. & A. M. of California for the fiscal year ended July 31, 1948 and present
herewith the following statements:
Grand Lodge Funds
Exhibit A: Statement of Grand Lodge cash received and disbursed by the
Grand Secretary and Grand Treasurer, August 1, 1947 to July 31, 1948.
Grand Secretarys Accounts
Exhibit B: Resume of cash received, August 1, 1947 to July 31, 1948.
Schedule 1: ·statement of Grand Lodge per capita dues collected from
1947 annual returns.
Schedule 2: Statement of Masonic Homes $25 contributions collected during the year 1947-48.
Schedule 3: Comparison of Budget and Expenditures, 1947-48.
Grand Treasurer's Accounts
Exhibit C: Statement of cash receipts and disbursements, August 1, 1947
to July 31, 1948.
Exhibit D: Statement of assets and liabilities, July 31, 1948.
Exhibit E: Statement of cash receipts and disbursements, War Relief
Fund, August 1. 1947 to July 31, 1948.
Exhibit F: List of securiites, July 31, 1948.
Comments
The revenue from per capita dues and other sources exceeded the expenses and appropriations by $31,372.29 as shown by Exhibit D. This excess
revenue was computed without deducting the $12,578.00 paid to Gravel Range
Lodge No. 59, the payment being classified as an account receivable in our
report.
All per capita dues, as reported on the 1947 annual returns from constituent Lodges, have been prud in full. Our Schedules 1 and 2 show proof of
the revenue due from the Lodges in accordance with their 1947 returns and
the $25.00 Homes contributions reports for the first three quarters of the fiscal
year 1947-48. The total revenue due, as shown, agrees with the total cash
received from the Lodges by the Grand Secretary.
Cash receipts were accounted for and traced to the proper depositories.
Disbursements were made by checks and supported by vouchers properly
approved by the Committee on Accounts. All bank balances were verified
by correspondence with the depositories. Certified list of the securities were
received from the Anglo California National Bank which holds the securities .
for safe-keeping. The securities as recorded in the books of account were
checked to these lists and found to be in agreement. All interest and dividends
due thereon were received and accounted for. $90,000.00 of U. S. Treasury
Bonds, due 1970 and 1972 were sold and $90,000.00 of U. S. Savings Bonds,
series G, due 1960 were purchased, during the year.
The War Relief Fund, amounting to $158,507.44, was transferred to the
General Fund of Grand Lodge and earmarked for future disposition by
Grand Lodge, in accordance with the recommendation adopted at the 1947
communication of Grand Lodge.
We show on our Statement of Assets and Liabilities, Exhibit D, under
Liabilities, the amount of $29,026.45 due to George Washington Masonic
National Memorial Fund by Grand Lodge. This amount is made up of the
per capita levy of 15c assessed on the 1947 annual returns and $4,511.00
collected from the $1.00 initiates' contributions, less $1,255.00 of the $1.00
contributions which was sent to the Fund during the year.
We certify that, in our opinion, the attached statements fairly present the
financial condition of the Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California as at July 31,
1948 and the result of its operations for the fiscal year 1947-48.
Respectfully submitted,
BURROWS, PARKER & COMPANY,
Certified Public Accountants.
Walter A. Parker.

the Masonic Homes report shows that this fund had a balance of $23,427.20

September 24, 1948
Grand Lodge F. & A M. of California
San Francisco, California
Gentlemen:
We have audited the accounts and records of the Masonic Homes Endowment Fund for the fiscal year ended July 31, 1948 and submit herewith the
following statements:
Exhibit A: Statement of Cash Receipts and Disbursements, August 1, 1947
to July 31, 1948.
Exhibit B: Statement of Endowment Fund Assets, July 31, 1948.
Exhibit C: Statement of John and Lena Luckenbach Fund, July 31, 1948.
Exhibit D: Statement of Income and Capital Accounts, for the fiscal year
ended July 31, 1948.
•
Schedule 1: Securities on hand, acquired prior to July 31, 1947.
Schedule 2: Securities received and purchased during the fiscal year ended
July 31, 1948.
Schedule 3: Statement of securities redeemed and sold.
COMMENTS
Cash:
The bank balances were verified by correspondence with the depositaries.
All interest and dividends due from investments and savings bank accounts
were received and turned over to the Masonic Homes. The total income received by the Homes from the Endowment and Luckenbach Funds amounted
to $79,061.79.
Securities:
Securities on hand that were acquired in prior years are listed on Schedule 1. Securities received through contributions and bequests, ,a nd bonds
purchased during the current year are listed on Schedule 2. Securities redeemed and sold during the current year are listed on Schedule 3.
Bonds purchased are listed at actual cost. Donated securities are listed at
market value when received, or at a nominal value of $1.00 if the actual value
is unknown.
Certified lists of securities held for the account of the Endowment Fund
were received from the Anglo California National Bank. The records were
checked to these lists and the securities not listed were found in the office
of the Grand Secretary and were inspected by us.
Increase in Fund:
The combined assets of the Endowment Fund and the Luckenbach Fund
show the following increase for the current year:

Comments
Cash:
All recorded receipts were properly accounted for and deposited in the
proper funds bank account. The bank balances were verified by correspondence with the depositaries.
·
Securities:
·
All stocks, bonds, ·real estate, life insurance policies and other properties
that had been donated to the Homes by applicants were transferred from the
Masonic Homes General Fund to the Decato Monthly Grant Fund during the
current year. Heretofore, only the income from such property, the proceeds
from sales, and actual cash donations from applicants were turned over to
the Monthly Grant Fund. It is the Monthly Grant Fund that provides the
money to pay the Decato residents their monthly cash allowance.
The securities remaining in the Masonic Homes General Fund are government bonds purchased from the General Fund, and are listed at actual
cost. The real estate is a piece of property donated to the general fund of
the Homes. The bonds were verified by a certified list from the Anglo California National Bank which holds them for safe-keeping.
Other Funds:
The Masonic Homes has numerous separate funds which have been created for definite or special purposes. Some were created by donation and by
bequest to the Homes and others by action of the Board of Trustees to set
aside money that is to be used only for the purpose indicated by the title of
the fund. Full details of these funds are shown on the attached statements
Schedules B-2 to B-14, inclusive.
'
All interest and dividends due on these funds were received, unless otherwise noted on the fund statement, and deposited in the proper bank accounts.

Payments due from the annuity funds in accordance with the contracts and
agreements, were made.
All bank balances were verified by correspondence with the depositaries.
The securities were accounted for as held ·by the Anglo California National
Bank, or in the office of the Grand Secretary. Those held by the bank were
verified by a certified list from the bank, and those in the office of the Grand
Secretary were inspected.

Sufficient examination and tests were made of the revenue and expense
accounts to satisfy ourselves as to the .g eneral correctness of the accounting
records. All interest due on the investments was received. The Endowment
Fund interest received is in agreement with the Endowment Fund audit report. Detailed distribution of the operating expenses of the two homes was
made by the Decoto and Covina offices and were accepted as correct after
we had verified amounts by totals. Disbursements were made by checks and
supported by proper vouchers.
The 1947 annual returns from the Lodges were audited and the $25.00
contributions due thereon, plus the contributions received during the first
three quarters of the current year, agreed with the amount turned over to
the Treasurer of the Hornes by the Grand Secretary. There was no per capita
levy this year.
The operations of the Masonic Homes resulted in a loss of $26,796.07 for
the current year, as shown by our Exhibit C. The overall expenses increased
$90,000.00 over last year, while the revenue decreased $145,000.00. The main
loss of revenue came through the elimination of the per capita levy and a
decrease of $75,000.00 in the $25.00 contributions.

accompanying statements present fairly the financial condition of the
Masonic Homes of California as at July 31, 1948, and the results of its operations for the year 1947-48.
